title: Grateful Dead Live at Newcastle-Under-Lyme on 1970-05-24
lineage: SBD MR > Cass > DAT > CD + AUD MR > Cass > DAT > CD patches

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality matrix recording of the Dead’s first European gig, rescued by a scorching Dark Star, monster The Other One and killer Me & My Uncle
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – Dark Star, The Other One, China Cat > Rider and Me & My Uncle are repeatedly called top‑tier for 1970.  The soundboard‑plus‑audience mix degrades after the first set (hum, tube overload and a weak Lovelight mix), but listeners still find it listenable and historically exciting.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars for its historic energy and standout jams, while noting only moderate recording flaws; weighted average yields ~4.1.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Soundboard patched with audience source; early mix OK but tubes hot, levels peaking, hum and occasional drop‑outs especially into Lovelight; overall listenable despite degradation.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First European appearance, high energy from the opening Casey Jones through to Lovelight; occasional mix issues later but the band stays on fire, delivering historic first‑time UK festival momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as electric, energetic and wacked/antsy early, then delivering killer solos on Dark Star and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is thin at the start, rolls in later; some tone distortion noted but generally solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong rhythm guitar and vocal work on Me & My Uncle; praised for complementing Jerry’s leads.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ runs wild, especially on Lovelight where he “takes the helm”; his playing is a highlight for fans.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s kick drum noted as powerful and close‑to‑stage; overall drumming described as massive and driving.
